items.title: Third US-Africa Frontiers of Science, Engineering, and Medicine Symposium (Feb 2025)
items.summary: PI Lukuyu participated in the Third U.S.-Africa Frontiers of Science, Engineering, and Medicine Symposium , held from February 18–20, 2025, in Kigali, Rwanda. Hosted by the U.S. National Academies in partnership with the Republic of Rwanda, the symposium brought together early- and mid-career researchers from across the U.S. and Africa to explore interdisciplinary solutions to global challenges. The event featured sessions on decarbonization, precision agriculture, biotechnology, space research, and smart cities, with opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange across borders and disciplines.

items.title: eGUIDE Annual Retreat in Rochester NY: September 12-14, 2024
items.summary: We had the pleasure of participating in the annual eGUIDE retreat at the Rochester Institute of Technology, which provided a fantastic opportunity to connect with both new and returning eGUIDE members. The retreat commenced with an enlightening visit to the Niagara Power Vista, where attendees gained valuable insights into hydropower energy generation, followed by a visit to the breathtaking Niagara Falls State Park. During the retreat, Ahana and Kwame showcased their ongoing research through poster presentations, fostering engaging discussions among participants.

items.title: New York City Climate Week: September 2024
items.summary: June Lukuyu attended several events during NYC Climate Week , including Climate Change AI and Google DeepMind’s event, AI for Climate Action: From Data to Impact . At this event, she delivered a lightning talk titled " Enabling Smart Grids for Climate Resilience & Adaptation in Africa " to showcase their CCAI-sponsored project, alongside a panel discussion featuring collaborator Genevieve Flasplohler.

items.title: Kigali Data Collection: August 2024
items.summary: Miquilina Anagbah led data collection for the project: Multi-Stakeholder Perspectives of Electric Bus Service in Kigali, Rwanda. in collaboration with students from the University of Rwanda, College of Science and Technology. We conducted surveys with about 800 electric and diesel bus passengers across Kigali to collect information on bus service satisfaction and perception of electric buses. This project is supported by BasiGO and USAID.

items.title: Summer 2024 Undergraduate Research Experience
items.summary: We had the pleasure of welcoming Biniyam Gebreyohannes, a fellow from the UW Clean Energy Bridge to Research Program (CEBR), and Lillian Nguyen, a Clean Energy Institute ALVA fellow, for their Summer Research Experience. Biniyam explored how weather patterns affect Minigrid electricity behavior, drawing insights from the Katiirwe solar Minigrid in Western Uganda. Meanwhile, Lillian investigated Climate and Energy Injustice, focusing on racial and income disparities in access to indoor comfort. They were mentored by Ahana, Kwame, and Miquilina.
